_comment: One TTFV receipt per reader per track. Fill by hand following docs/measurement/ttfv-protocol.md; delete no keys. Null means not reached, not applicable, or unknown. Save as docs/measurement/receipts/YYYY-MM-DD-<handle>-<track>.json. track: demo | own-agent. date: YYYY-MM-DD of the attempt. facilitator: a handle only, no personal data. network: yes | no, whether the machine had internet access during the attempt; required yes for Track A and for uv tool install; checked once before the clock starts (protocol 2.7). coaching_events: list of {"at", "what"}. failures: list of {"at", "milestone", "what"}, kept even when the attempt failed.

reader._comment: handle: a public handle, no other personal data. kind: cold | maintainer | ai-agent; only cold receipts without coaching events count toward cold-reader metrics.

machine._comment: os and cpu as reported by the system (e.g. uname -sr, CPU model and core count); python and uv are `python3 --version` and `uv --version`. uv_cache: cold (fresh UV_CACHE_DIR) or warm.

package._comment: version: the agent-reliability-ci version installed. source: pypi or wheel. wheel_sha256: required when source is wheel (record UV_FIND_LINKS and any UV_CACHE_DIR in notes, protocol 2.3). readme_url: the README read, at a fixed commit.

project._comment: Track B only; null for demo. kind: own | sample. description: what the agent is, or which recipe the sample tree came from. refs_preexisting: baseline, candidate, toolset and oracle were importable before the clock started. workers: worker count of the run.

timestamps._comment: ISO 8601 with timezone, e.g. 2026-10-20T09:15:02Z. Track A uses readme_opened, command_start, demo_banner, demo_verdict, all_steps_held, interpretation_answered. Track B uses readme_opened, install_start, install_done, scaffold_start, descriptor_written, run_start, verdict_printed, store_validated, interpretation_answered. Leave the others null.

durations_seconds._comment: Whole seconds derived from the timestamps as the protocol defines per track (sections 3 and 4). agent_execution is Track B only: the sum of usage.wall_seconds over trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2), never subtracted from total.

outcome._comment: completed: every stop condition of the track held. verdict: PASS | BLOCK | INCONCLUSIVE | ERROR; Track B: the verdict stamped as verdict_printed; ERROR if none; Track A: the verdict for agent B. store_validated, decision_sha256, init_attempts, descriptor_hand_edited, trials_started: Track B only (protocol 4.3 and 4.6). descriptor_hand_edited: arci.yaml edited by hand before the run that produced the verdict, or, with no valid verdict, before any arci run that started trials. trials_started: trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2) exists and is non-empty. interpretation_correct is scored with the key in protocol 5.3.
outcome.interpretation_answer: Under a timeout fault on the first reserve call, with 200 trials per arm, agent B (A with the retry removed) succeeded 132/200 vs A's 192/200, and the upper confidence bound on the drop was worse than the 0.10 margin, so ARCI is confident B is meaningfully less reliable than A and the gate fails (exit 1). It is a relative verdict about this experiment, not a statement about either agent's absolute quality.

comprehension._comment: Answered once per reader, on the first track's receipt; on a second-track receipt set answered_on to that file name and leave the rest empty. Answers verbatim; scores per the key in protocol section 5; scorer is not the reader and is a handle only, no personal data. q2_who_for keeps its name for schema stability; it holds the whole q2 answer (who it is for and what the agent must expose).

answers.q1_what_is_it: ARCI is a CI-style regression gate for LLM/tool-using agents: it runs a baseline and a candidate version many times under the same pre-declared tasks and injected tool faults, grades each trial with a separate oracle over the final environment state, and returns PASS/BLOCK/INCONCLUSIVE/ERROR as an exit code (0/1/2/3). It can also diff a passing and failing trace, shrink the injected faults, and replay a recorded failure offline.
answers.q2_who_for: People who build agents and want to know whether a change (prompt, code, retry logic) made the agent less reliable before merging. The agent must route its tool calls through ARCI's boundary: either a Python function agent(task, tools, rng) -> dict calling tools.call(...), with a toolset factory (task, seed) -> object with .tools and .snapshot() and an oracle (task, final_state) -> bool, or a command agent that speaks MCP over stdio.
answers.q3_pass_means: PASS means only that, for this pre-declared experiment (task, faults, N, alpha, delta), the statistical lower bound on candidate-minus-baseline success rate is above -delta, i.e. any reliability drop is smaller than the allowed margin. It says nothing about absolute reliability.
answers.q4_does_not_do: It is not a sandbox or security boundary (agents are assumed buggy, not hostile). It only sees calls that cross its tool boundary (direct file/network/subprocess access is invisible), and it replays recorded boundary calls, not model inference, so a live-model bundle usually replays INVALID. Also: declaring a fault does not guarantee it was injected.
answers.q5_first_three_commands: 1) uv tool install agent-reliability-ci  2) arci init checkout-retry --baseline app.v1:run --candidate app.v2:run --toolset tests.world:make_world --oracle tests.world:passed  3) arci run arci.yaml. (In my case the install had to be `uv venv` + `uv pip install`, and init also needed `--task '{"order_id": "order-7"}'`.)

coaching_events.what: Before readme_opened (not stamped): the facilitator prompt stated that this harness blocks `uv tool install` and that uvx or a uv venv are alternatives; it also prescribed the timestamping wrapper and the milestone names. No explanation of ARCI was given.

notes:
Command used: cd $(mktemp -d) [= <tmp>]; uvx --from agent-reliability-ci arci demo 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r l; do printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$l"; done | tee demo.log; echo "exit: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}". Log: <tmp>/demo.log. Reader's verdict line for agent B: VERDICT: BLOCK (exit 1)   [A vs agent_b]  (A 192/200, agent_b 132/200, matches the recorded run). The stamped attempt's exit code was not captured (the facilitator's wrapper used bash's PIPESTATUS under zsh), so exit_code and completed are null; the reader re-ran the demo under bash outside the clock and reported exit 0 (see failures). interpretation_answered not stamped (answers given after both tracks). AI-agent reader (Claude opus via the Workflow tool, persona: an ML engineer who builds LLM agents with tool calls and evaluates them with ad-hoc scripts); self-stamped milestones with `date -u` under the facilitator's wrapper; machine shared with the orchestrator session (not controlled). Never counted as a cold reader. Protocol 2.1 deviation: the maintainer checkout was present on the machine; the reader read README.md from it and Track B copied the sample tree from it (no clone was made by the reader). Files read: README.md, <tmp>/arci.yaml (generated by arci init), directory listing only of the copied sample project (app/__init__.py, v1.py, v2.py, tests/__init__.py, world.py, README.md were not opened). Confusions: The README's 'Gate your own agent' commands do not mention --task, but the sample toolset needs a task with order_id; init failed with KeyError: 'order_id' until I guessed --task '{"order_id": "order-7"}' from the hand-written YAML example. A first-timer would not know which task keys their own toolset expects to be required here. | The README one-liner chains `uv tool install ... && arci init ... && arci run ...`, which assumes arci lands on PATH; with any other install route (venv) I had to call .venv/bin/arci. | Without --fault the scaffold runs a 'clean' condition only, so the run did not actually exercise v1 vs v2 under the retry-relevant fault; both arms were 8/8. It was unclear from the README whether I was supposed to add --fault tool_timeout:reserve for the 'checkout-retry' example; I followed the commands as written. | The README is long and dense (Jev decision endpoint, calibration audit, evalopt independence) before reaching 'Gate your own agent'; the part I needed was near the bottom. | Track A wrapper uses ${PIPESTATUS[0]}, which is empty under zsh (this machine's shell), so the first demo run printed 'exit: ' with no code; I re-ran the demo under bash to get the exit code. | The venv was created with CPython 3.13.12 although the task said 3.14 is on PATH; uv picked it on its own. Not a problem, just unexpected. Reader notes: Timings: demo 12:09:52Z -> 12:11:05Z (~73 s, including uvx env resolution; first output after ~1 s, so the package was apparently already cached); rerun 75 s. Own-agent path: install 1 s (packages resolved from uv cache in 1 ms, so this is not a cold-network install), scaffold 6 s including one failure and retry, run 2 s. Total README-open to own verdict ~107 s. Demo counts matched recorded run (A 192/200, B 132/200, A-vs-A 192/200, C PASS). Decision.json sha256 unchanged after `arci gate`, and gate reproduced INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2). Machine state: load average 8.46 / 5.99 / 3.79 at 12:12:59Z, consistent with other agents running in parallel; no lingering arci/pytest processes found by ps at that moment. The uv cache was warm (installs took milliseconds), so install timing is not representative of a true first visitor. I did not open any docs/ file, the sample project's own README, or its source files; I did not read the generated store files beyond listing and hashing. I did not run arci plan or add a fault, so my own run says nothing about v1 vs v2 under a timeout. Scorer rationale: All five answers contain every required element, so nothing is missing.

- q1: The answer compares baseline and candidate, runs both many times under the same pre-declared tasks and injected faults, and returns PASS/BLOCK/INCONCLUSIVE/ERROR as an exit code usable in CI.
- q2: It names people changing an agent who want to know about a reliability regression before merging. It names both integration routes: the Python function agent(task, tools, rng) and the MCP-over-stdio command.
- q3: It says PASS is relative to the baseline, and that the lower bound on candidate-minus-baseline is above -delta. It limits this to the pre-declared experiment and says it is not a claim of absolute reliability.
- q4: It gives at least two distinct README limits: not a sandbox or security boundary, only calls across its tool boundary are seen, and boundary calls are replayed, not model inference.
- q5: The three commands are in order: uv tool install agent-reliability-ci, then arci init with --baseline/--candidate/--toolset/--oracle, then arci run arci.yaml. The extra note about a venv workaround and --task is a caveat, not a wrong claim.
- Demo-block interpretation (BLOCK): The candidate is meaningfully worse than the baseline by more than the 0.10 margin. The answer frames this as a relative verdict about this experiment, not absolute quality. The upper-bound wording is loose but not wrong.
- Own-run interpretation (INCONCLUSIVE): The answer says there is not enough evidence either way, with no regression claimed and no pass claimed. It also mentions arci plan for a larger run. This matches the verdict line INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2).

failures.what: Wrapper printed "exit: " with no value because ${PIPESTATUS[0]} is not set in zsh. Re-ran `uvx --from agent-reliability-ci arci demo` under bash -c from 2026-10-13T12:11:44Z to 2026-10-13T12:12:59Z (log demo2.log in the same temp dir): exit 0.
